title: fix(plugin-audit)!: a comment's display name is stamped from the caller's session, like its author id
body:
Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no skill or doc teaches a client to write a comment's display fields; the one docs example (`content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-detail.mdx`) reads `author_name`, which is unchanged.

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:评论的显示名与头像(`author_name` / `author_avatar_url`)改由服务端在创建时按当前会话用户自己的资料(`sys_user` 的名称与 `image`)写入,与 `author_id` 同源;编辑时这两个字段只读,保持创建时的值。系统上下文写入(种子、导入、迁移)不变。
- **为什么改**:评论的显示身份应与作者 id 一样是服务端事实,读者看到的名字只能是作者本人的。
- **风险与回滚**:收窄(请求里带的这两个字段不再落库);控制台无需改动。直接调用 `installCommentAccessHooks` 而不传解析器的宿主,新评论不带显示名(安装时 warn 一次)。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- **先看**:`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-access-hooks.ts`(创建钩子末尾的盖章段与 `authorIdentityOf`)、`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-comment.object.ts`(两字段 `readonly`)、`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-plugin.ts`(解析器接线)。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run test/comment-author-display-identity.dogfood.test.ts`,预期 `Tests 3 passed (3)`。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地。

## What changes

A comment's display name is stamped from the caller's session, like its author id.

- **Create.** The `sys_comment` create hook (`installCommentAccessHooks`) assigns `author_name` and `author_avatar_url` from the session user's own `sys_user` profile, the title column and `image`, after the comment is admitted, whether or not the request carries them. A user whose profile cannot be read is stored with neither. The resolution is the audit writers' actor snapshot, the one the record history's actor columns are written with: `installAuditWriters` now returns a handle with `resolveActorSnapshot(api, userId)`, and `AuditPlugin` passes it to `installCommentAccessHooks` as a new optional sixth argument, `resolveAuthorIdentity`.
- **Update.** Both fields declare `readonly: true` on `sys_comment`, so the engine's update-side strip drops a non-system caller's value and reports it in `droppedFields` and `X-ObjectStack-Dropped-Fields`. The write is never refused, and an edit, the author's or a parent editor's, never changes whose name a comment shows.
- **Unchanged.** `author_id` keeps its rules. System-context writes keep the values they supply. Stored comments keep what they were written with. The console's create payload is accepted as before, and its display fields are assigned over.
- **Also.** A comment posted with no display name (REST, MCP, agent) now shows its author's name instead of none, and the @mention notification title names that author.

## Tests

All readings below are at `dde4c9f4b` unless a line says otherwise.

- New `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-author-display-identity.integration.test.ts`, real kernel, ObjectQL, AuditPlugin and SQLite, with the platform's `sys_user`: the caller's own name and avatar are stored whatever the request carries; a comment with none sent is stamped (the control); an unreadable profile stores neither; an update strips both and reports them; a parent editor's edit keeps the author's; a system write keeps its own.
- New `packages/qa/dogfood/test/comment-author-display-identity.dogfood.test.ts`, at the REST data door of a booted stack: the served comment shows the caller's own name and avatar whatever the request carries; control: an ordinary comment shows its caller's own name, for each of two callers; a PATCH naming both fields answers 200, `droppedFields` names them with reason `readonly`, the body edit lands, and the served identity is unchanged.
- Repaired `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-write-locale-settings-seam.integration.test.ts`: it named its mention actor through a display name in the create request, which this change no longer stores; it now seeds the author's `sys_user` profile. Its four assertions are unchanged.

## Acceptance notes

- The display identity is a snapshot taken at creation, read through the actor snapshot (at most one `sys_user` read per user per 30 s window). A rename or a new avatar shows on comments created after the window; existing comments keep what they were created with, as record history entries do.
- A host that installs the comment hooks itself without `resolveAuthorIdentity` stores no display identity on new comments, never the request's, and is told once at install, at `warn`.
